name: Alglucosidase alfa

discovery.by: Yuan-Tsong Chen and colleagues, Duke University
discovery.note: Recombinant acid alpha-glucosidase produced in CHO cells showed glycogen clearance in animal models of Pompe disease.

tagline: First treatment for Pompe disease, a fatal glycogen storage disorder of muscle
summary: Alglucosidase alfa is recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase that is taken up into muscle lysosomes and breaks down glycogen. Approved in 2006, it was the first therapy for Pompe disease and markedly improves survival in infantile-onset disease. It carries boxed warnings for anaphylaxis and immune-mediated reactions.
mechanism: Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II) results from deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase, which degrades glycogen. Glycogen accumulates in cardiac, skeletal and respiratory muscle, causing cardiomyopathy and progressive weakness.

Alglucosidase alfa carries mannose-6-phosphate residues that bind the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor on muscle cells, which internalise it to lysosomes where it hydrolyses glycogen. Uptake into skeletal muscle is relatively inefficient, which motivated later enzymes with more mannose-6-phosphate.
uses: Pompe disease (acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency), infantile and late onset

history.title: Novazyme
history.detail: Genzyme acquires Novazyme, co-founded by John Crowley, whose children had Pompe disease, adding to its Duke-derived enzyme programme.

history.title: First approvals
history.detail: Myozyme is authorised in the EU in March and by the FDA in April for Pompe disease.

history.title: Lumizyme
history.detail: FDA approves the larger-scale Lumizyme product for late-onset disease, later for all patients.

history.title: Film
history.detail: The film Extraordinary Measures dramatises the Crowley family's efforts.

history.title: Successor enzyme
history.detail: Sanofi's avalglucosidase alfa (Nexviazyme), with increased mannose-6-phosphate, is approved.

serious: acute cardiorespiratory failure from fluid overload
safety.boxed_warning: Life-threatening anaphylaxis, hypersensitivity and immune-mediated reactions; risk of acute cardiorespiratory failure in patients with compromised cardiac or respiratory function.
